questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All blacks are blues.

All blues are pinks.

No pink is a green.

**Conclusions:**

1. All greens can be blues.

2. Some pinks are blacks.

3. All blacks are greens.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cd808741befa7d8cfb9cf1daf25fbca1a4e0a314b8a08b8c3a1646469f95396.png] 

Conclusions:

 
• All greens can be blues → Does not follow (As all blues are pinks and no pink is a green. So, whole blues comes in pinks which can not be green, therefore it is definitely false)
 
• Some pinks are blacks → Follow (As all blacks are blues and all blues are pinks. So, as whole blacks comes in blues which whole comes in pinks therefore it is definitely true)
 
• All blacks are greens → Does not follow (As all blacks are blues, all blues are pinks and no pink is a green. So, as whole blacks comes in blues which whole comes in pinks which can not be green, therefore it is definitely false)

∴ Here, Only conclusion 2 follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusion 2 follows".

questions.question: If loan exposure is supported by collateral, it’s said to be ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**secured credit.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secured credit** is a type of loan that is **backed by collateral. **
 
• Secured credit is commonly used for **mortgages, auto loans, and secured credit cards.**
 
• Secured credit is considered **less risky for lenders** because they have a way to recover their money if the borrower defaults on the loan. This makes it **easier for borrowers** **with poor credit to get approved for a loan**.
 
• **Collateral is an asset** that the borrower **pledges as security for the loan**. 
 
 
• **Collateral **can take many forms, including **real estate, vehicles, stocks, and jewellery**. 
 
• If the borrower defaults on the loan, the lender can seize the collateral to recover the amount owed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unsecured credit** is a type of loan which are **not backed by collateral**. Lenders rely on the borrower's creditworthiness to determine if they will be able to repay the loan. Unsecured credit is considered **riskier for lenders** and therefore, typically comes with **higher interest rates.**

 
 
• **Unsecured credit** is commonly used for **credit cards, personal loans, and student loans.**
 
 
 
• **Poor credit** refers to a** low credit score or a history of missed payments and defaults**. Borrowers with poor credit may have difficulty getting approved for loans or may be **charged higher interest rates to compensate for the increased risk.**
 
• **High credit **refers to a **good credit score and a history of responsible credit management.** Borrowers with high credit are more likely to be approved for loans and may be **offered lower interest rates.**

questions.question: Statutory body of higher education, which was set up during the first five year plan in India, ______.

• **University Grants Commission (UGC)** came into existence on **28 December 1953** under **the first five-year plan in India** to promote and coordinate university education.
 
• It became** a statutory body** under **University Grants Commission Act 1956.**
 
• It is the main **regulatory body for higher education** in India.
 
• It is responsible for providing recognition to universities in India and disbursing funds to them for development and research purposes.
 
• It sets quality standards for higher education institutions in India and monitors their compliance.
 
• It also provides financial assistance to universities and colleges for the development of infrastructure and research facilities.
 
• In **2018**, UGC was **replaced by the Higher Education Commission of India (HECI)** which will act as a single regulator for higher education institutions in India. However, the proposal is** yet to be implemented.**

• It was later reconstituted as **a statutory body** under the **Indian Medical Council Act, 1956** which replaced the earlier Act.
 
• It was **regulating medical education and profession** in India.

questions.question: The north-west part of India receives rainfall in winter due to ______.

__
 
• **Western Disturbances** are low-pressure systems that** originate in the Mediterranean region** and move towards the Indian subcontinent.
 
• These disturbances **bring rainfall to the north-western parts of India during **the** winter** months, and they also affect the weather conditions in other parts of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The South-west monsoon** is the **primary rainy season in India**, which** starts in** **June and lasts till September**.

 
 
• This monsoon is** caused by** the differential heating of land and sea, which results in the formation of** low-pressure systems over the Indian Ocean and the Arabian Sea.**
 
 
 
• **The North-east is** known as the **winter monsoon**, the northeast monsoon approaches India from the northeast.
 
 
• During this time, rainfall is common throughout the southern region of India, particularly in Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **The Retreating Monsoon**, also **known **as the **North-East monsoon,** brings** rainfall to the southern parts of India during October and November.**
 
 
• This monsoon is **caused by the withdrawal of the south-west monsoon winds** and the formation of a low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Humus, a dark colored amorphous substance is formed as a result of which process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humification.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humus **is a dark-colored, amorphous substance that is** formed due to the process of humification.**

 
 
• **Humification **is the process by which dead organic matter, such as leaves, twigs, and other plant and animal remains, are broken down by microorganisms and transformed into humus.
 
 
 
• It is an important component of soil, as it improves soil fertility, water retention, and nutrient availability.
 
• It is **a complex mixture of organic compounds**, including **humic acids**,** fulvic acids**, and **humin**.
 
 
• **Humic acids** are the most abundant and important component of humus, and they play a key role in soil fertility by improving soil structure, nutrient availability, and water retention.
 
• **Fulvic acids** are smaller and more soluble than humic acids, and they are involved in the transport of nutrients and other substances within the soil.
 
• **Humin** is a highly stable component of humus that is resistant to further decomposition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fragmentation **is the process by which large pieces of organic matter are broken down into smaller pieces, but it does not result in the formation of humus.
 
• **Leaching **is the process by which water carries dissolved nutrients and other substances from the soil surface to deeper layers, but it does not result in the formation of humus.
 
• **Mineralization **is the process by which microorganisms break down organic matter and release nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur into the soil to be easily available forms to plants.

questions.question: Dev and Rohit can do a work in 12 and 36 days, respectively. Starting with Dev, they work on alternate days. When will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
**Data:**

Dev can complete work in 12 days,

Rohit can complete work in 36 days.

**Concept:**

If Dev completes 1/12th of the work on the first day, Rohit will complete 1/36th of the work on the second day, and so forth.

**Solution:**

Dev's work rate: 1/12 work/day,

Rohit's work rate: 1/36 work/day,

Work done in 2 days: 1/12 + 1/36 = 1/9,

Number of days to complete work: 2 × (9) = 18 days.

**Therefore, the work will be completed in 18 days.**

questions.question: If the number 715*42324 is completely divisible by 3, then find the largest whole number in the place of *,
questions.solution:
**Data:**

715*42324, * can be any digit.

**Concept:**

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

**Solution:**

Sum of digits: 7 + 1 + 5 + * + 4 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 4 = 28 + *,

⇒ * must be 2 or 5 or 8 for 71542324 to be divisible by 3.

The largest digit among 2, 5, and 8 is 8.

**Hence, the largest whole number in place of * is 8.**

questions.question: Ashok bought a laptop for ₹60,000 and sold it for ₹72,000. What is the percentage profit on the sale of laptop?

Profit % = (Profit/Cost Price) × 100.

questions.question: In a race of 500 meters, Q can give a head start of 50 meters to P and R can give a head start of 100 meters to Q to complete the race at the same time. Find the head start that R can give to P to complete this race at the same time.
questions.solution:

Race length = 500m,

Q can give a head start of 50m to P,

R can give a head start of 100m to Q.

**Concept:**

In a race, if two competitors finish at the same time and one has a head start, the one without the head start is faster. This can be extrapolated to calculate head starts between different pairs of competitors.

**Solution:**

R's speed relative to Q's speed = 500/400 = 1.25,

R's speed relative to P's speed = 1.25 × (500/450) = 1.3889,

Head start R can give P = 500 - (500/1.3889) = 140m.

**Therefore, R can give a head start of 140 meters to P to complete the race at the same time.**

questions.question: A sum on compound interest amounts to Rs.2,809 in 2 years and Rs.2,977.54 in 3 years. The rate per cent per annum is:

Compound Interest for the 3rd year = Rs.2977.54 - Rs.2809 = Rs.168.54,

Rate = (168.54/2809) × 100 = 6%.

**Therefore, the rate per cent per annum is 6%.**

questions.question: Somaraj borrowed an amount of Rs.11,550 at an interest rate of 10% per annum, compounded annually. He paid the entire amount in two equal annual instalments. What is the value of each installment?
questions.solution:
**Given data :**

Principal (P) = Rs 11,550

Interest rate (r) = 10% per annum

Compound frequency (n) = 1 time per year

Time (t) = 2 years

Two equal instalments (P1 and P2)

**Concept:**

The principal plus accrued interest after one year minus the first installment equals the second installment after it accrues interest for one year.

**Solution:**

Calculate the compounded amount after 1 year: P × (1 + r/n)^(nt) ⇒ Rs 11,550 × (1 + 10/100)^(1 × 1) ⇒ Rs 12,705

Let each instalment be X.

Substituting this in our equation gives the balance after the first payment: Rs 12,705 - X

This balance will accrue interest over the next year,

⇒ (Rs 12,705 - X) × (1 + 10/100) ⇒ X

⇒ 1.1 × (Rs 12,705 - X) = X

⇒ 1.1X + X = Rs 13,975.5

⇒ 2.1X = Rs 13,975.5

⇒ X = Rs 13,975.5 / 2.1

⇒ X = (1.1 × Rs 12,705) / 2.1 ⇒ X = Rs 6,655

**Therefore, each instalment would be Rs 6655.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__****Formula Used:**

Where P = Principal, x = equal installments, and r = rate of interest

**Calculation:**

According to the formula,

11550 = (x)/(1+frac{10){100}}+(x)/((1+frac{10){100})²}

⇒ 11550 = (10x/11) + (100x/121)

⇒ 1155 = 21x/121

⇒ x = 6655

**∴ Each installment is Rs. 6655**

questions.question: 4 years ago, the average age of a family of 4 members was 16 years. A baby is born today. What will be the present average age of 5 members of the family?
questions.solution:
**Data:**

Average age of a family of 4 members 4 years ago = 16 years.

**Concept:**

The current average age is calculated by adding the years passed to the old average, and the average age after adding a new member is calculated by dividing the total age by the number of members.

**Solution:**

Current average age = 16 + 4 = 20 years,

Total age of family now = 20 × 4 = 80 years,

Average age after the baby is born = (80 + 0) / 5 = 16 years.

**Therefore, the present average age of the family of 5 members is 16 years.**
